section: 2. Two layers and one question: where does the control signal enter?
text: The two layers use some of the same injection mechanisms (cross-attention, adaptive normalisation, token conditioning, guidance at sampling time; a ControlNet-style branch is common at the sensor level and appears at the scenario level only in one rendering stage [124]) but differ in what the signal means: a risk level, a goal point or a language clause at the scenario level; an ego pose, a box layout or a weather prompt at the sensor level.
previous_sentence: **Sensor level (64 papers).** The families are defined by the signal: ego action or trajectory (19), layout, box, map or BEV conditioning (16), unified multi-condition control (16), text or language (4), inference-time guidance or editing (3), prediction without a control input (2), other (2), camera or viewpoint (1) and scenario, risk or event conditioning (1). 20 of the 64 are from 2024, 23 from 2025 and 17 from 2026.

section: 6. Cross-cutting findings
text: **Control is often measured indirectly, most clearly at the sensor level.** At the sensor level the common evidence is a downstream or fidelity number (perception on generated data, FID and FVD) rather than a measurement of whether the output follows the specified signal; the four analyses in section 4.3 show why the distinction matters.

section: 6. Cross-cutting findings
text: **Language control is a mixture of three designs.** Text can be turned into code or a loss [13][76], trained in directly [73][10], or used to edit a scene [48]; the limitations stated for them differ where they are stated at all, and direct adherence measurements exist for some (clause satisfaction in [10], command execution success in [48]) but not for most.
previous_sentence: **Much "control" at the scenario level is an objective.** Adversarial purpose dominates among the papers labelled controllable (section 3.5), and many reported benefits are for the planner trained on the data, not for the user who specifies the scenario.

section: 6. Cross-cutting findings
text: **No shared yardstick for control.** The rows use different data, metrics and baselines; some setups recur (nuScenes FID and FVD at the sensor level, Waymo sim-agent realism scores at the scenario level), but the control measurements are not on a common benchmark, so this survey does not rank methods.
previous_sentence: **Closed-loop use is the direction of travel but the evidence is thin.** Both the company statements and the academic rows point to closed-loop evaluation and training, yet only eight of 64 world-model rows run a closed loop and three of those are qualitative.
